{{Quote|But wesa still needen our beasts, to carry weapons and shields. The evil mackineecks had captured the beasts, for killin' and skinnin'. As the Queen and her big brains plan a big nasty, wesa attacking Camp Six, to rescue our animals and complete disen Gungan Grand Army.|[[Boss/Legends|Boss]] [[Rugor Nass/Legends|Rugor Nass]] in a journal entry|<ref name="SW:GB">''[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds]]''</ref>}}
'''Fambaas''' were herbivorous [[Amphibian/Legends|amphibians]] native to the [[Gungan Swamp|swamps]] of the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]].

The largest terrestrial herbivores of the swamp, fambaas were technically amphibians but had the scaly hide of [[Reptile/Legends|reptiles]]. The creatures were native to the [[Lianorm Swamp/Legends|Gungan Swamps]] of Naboo and the jungles of [[Onderon/Legends|Onderon]].

==Biology and appearances==
{{Quote|I know how you feel. You lost your master, and I lost my Jedi.|[[Hondo Ohnaka/Legends|Hondo Ohnaka]] to Preigo's fambaa|<ref name="TCW:BFR">{{TCW|Bound for Rescue}}</ref>}}
[[File:Fambaa-woswfg.jpg|thumb|left|180px|Wild fambaas foraging for food.]]
Fambaas were large [[Sentience/Legends|non-sentient]] [[Amphibian/Legends|amphibians]] native to the [[Gungan/Legends|Gungan]] swamps of the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]], that could also be found on [[Onderon/Legends|Onderon]].<ref name="SWE">{{SW|url=explore/the-clone-wars/ep502|text="A War on Two Fronts" - ''The Clone Wars'' Episode Guide|nolive=1}} {{C|Slide 3}}</ref> They obtained food by easily knocking over trees to get at leaves and berries. They also foraged for underwater plants, breathing underwater and swimming with ease.<ref name="WSW" /> They reached sizes of up to 9 [[Meter/Legends|meters]].

In the wild, fambaas traveled in herds of up to twelve, but formed breeding herds of hundreds of family units that were so large they were traditionally put to pasture in sacred swampy areas. There were also special fambaa stables contained inside the underwater [[Hydrostatic bubble/Legends|hydrostatic bubble]]-enclosed cities for the domesticated breeds kept by Gungans. Females laid large numbers of sticky, gelatinous eggs, which they deposited in puddles and underwater. The young hatched with moist skin and gills, and upon maturity, the gills disappeared and their skin hardened.<ref name="WSW" />

The fambaas, though immense, were relatively docile herbivores who were only dangerous for their size and clumsiness.<ref name=":0">{{SWE|characters|fambaa|fambaa}}</ref> Their only known predators were [[Sando aqua monster/Legends|sando aqua monsters]] breaching the surface of the swamp waters from the abyssal ocean beneath.<ref name="WSW" />

==History==
[[File:Fambaaherd-woswfg.jpg|thumb|right|250px|A herd of wild fambaas]]
The fambaa had been domesticated by Gungans for millennia as beasts of burden and cavalry/artillery draft beasts.  In times of war, fambaas were used to carry portable [[Gungan shield generator|deflector shield generators]] for protecting their Gungan masters. They were also mounted with large [[Booma/Legends|booma]] cannons. During the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]] [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|occupation]]<ref name="SW:GB" /> of Naboo in [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]],<ref name="TNEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' places the [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|Invasion of Naboo]] in [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]].</ref> the fambaas were placed in [[Camp Six]]. They were subsequently [[Liberation of Harte Secur|released]] by the [[Gungan Grand Army/Legends|Gungan Grand Army]] and outfitted for use in the [[Battle of Naboo/Legends|the Gungan's diversionary battle]].<ref name="SW:GB" /> During that battle, the fambaa-mounted shield generator protected the Grand Army<ref name="Episode I">{{Film|I}}</ref> until the generators were destroyed by [[Battle droid/Legends|battle droids]],<ref name="Battlefront">''[[Star Wars: Battlefront]]''</ref> wounding the fambaa mounts.<ref name=":0" />

During their [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] [[Battle of Onderon/Legends|insurgency]], the [[Onderon rebels/Legends|Onderon rebels]] used fambaas to hold heavy artillery.<ref name="TCW:TP">{{TCW|Tipping Points}}</ref> In [[Abafar/Legends|Abafar]], they were used as meat in a dish known as [[Fambaa Delight/Legends|Fambaa Delight]].<ref name="TCW:MIA">{{TCW|Missing in Action}}</ref> Around that time, [[Preigo's Traveling World of Wonder/Legends|Preigo's Traveling World of Wonder]] had a fambaa as part of the performance. The beast was abandoned to the [[Ohnaka Gang/Legends|Ohnaka Gang]] when [[Preigo/Legends|Preigo]] and the other performers fled a [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] rescue mission.<ref name="TCW:BFR" />

During the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], [[Captain of the Line/Legends|Senior Captain]] [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo/Legends|Thrawn]] of the [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Navy]], tasked a experienced [[Spacer/Legends|spacer]] to kill an adult fambaa for him, then retrieve a vial blood sample in order for Thrawn to conduct a scientific experiment.

==Behind the scenes==
The original concept sketches of the fambaa were two-legged dinosaur-like creatures, lacking forelimbs like their [[Kaadu/Legends|kaadu]] cousins. Once the four-legged design was approved, concept artist [[Terryl Whitlatch]] developed a hand-drawn walk cycle to demonstrate to ILM animators how the animal should move.

In the [[2001]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds]]'' and its [[2002]] [[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds: Clone Campaigns|expansion pack]], fambaas were the Gungan special unit, used as a mobile shield generator. They were also used as the Gungan Assault Mech, armed with a powerful [[Booma/Legends|Booma]] cannon. For the sake of gameplay the Fambaa was the Gungan countermeasure to the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation's]] [[Multi-Troop Transport/Legends|Multi-Troop Transport]]. The shield generator-mounted ones were upgradeable with a heavier shield.<ref name="SW:GB" /><ref name="Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds: Clone Campaigns">''[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds: Clone Campaigns]]''</ref>
